1. Scientific Analysis

The 31P NMR series tracks the mixed G2/TEP Mg(OTf)2 electrolyte from 313.2 K down to 243.2 K. The dominant, robust finding is a slow-to-fast chemical-exchange transition governing TEP speciation. At low temperature (243.2, 258.2 K) three resolved 31P environments are present, with a very broad dominant component (FWHM up to 3.38 ppm) — the hallmark of intermediate/slow exchange between distinct TEP solvation states (free TEP near -5.5/-6 ppm and Mg-coordinated TEP near -3.5 ppm), plus an additional inner-shoulder environment resolved only by the 3-Voigt fit. Between 258.2 and 278.2 K the resolved-species count collapses to 1, and above this the single peak sharpens progressively (0.98→0.36→0.19 ppm) toward a motionally averaged fast-exchange resonance. The apparent 'dominant' chemical shift is non-monotonic (and its linear/Arrhenius regressions are near-meaningless, R²~0.15-0.19) precisely because the 'dominant' label maps to different physical entities across the coalescence — a coalesced population-weighted average at high T versus a resolved single environment at low T — so scatter there is expected rather than a fit failure. Fit quality improves monotonically with T as lineshapes simplify. The residual structure is physically informative and clusters in the transition region: at low T the residuals reflected genuine under-resolution (fixed by adding a component), while at mid T (278.2, 293.5 K) coherent single-sign-change dispersive S-shaped residuals straddle the apex. This asymmetry is consistent with incomplete coalescence (a not-quite-averaged shoulder) but is also the textbook signature of a small phase error; the F-test rejected an extra component and phase correction was outside the locked constraints, so these two explanations remain degenerate on the present data. The locked model's design (T-dependent Voigt count) matches the exchange interpretation and thereby captures the dominant physics well; relaxation narrowing (with T1 data available) may contribute to FWHM trends but cannot account for the species-count change and is therefore secondary. A key reporting limitation: no Larmor frequency was in the metadata, so FWHM is available only in ppm (not Hz) and no T2* estimate can be quoted, weakening quantitative separation of exchange vs relaxation contributions to linewidth.

5. Scientific Claims

Claim 1: The 31P NMR of the G2/TEP Mg(OTf)2 electrolyte undergoes a slow-to-fast chemical-exchange transition with increasing temperature: three resolved TEP-solvation environments at low T (243-258 K) coalesce into a single motionally-averaged, progressively narrowing resonance above ~278 K, evidencing temperature-controlled competitive solvation exchange between free and Mg-coordinated TEP.

Scientific Impact: Directly characterizes how temperature governs the speciation and solvation dynamics of the active cation in a mixed-solvent Mg electrolyte, which controls ion transport and coordination-shell composition relevant to battery performance.

Literature Search Query: Has anyone quantified the temperature-dependent exchange kinetics (coalescence temperature and exchange rate) between free and Mg-coordinated TEP in mixed diglyme/triethyl-phosphate Mg electrolytes using variable-temperature 31P NMR?

Keywords: 31P NMR, chemical exchange, coalescence, competitive solvation, Mg electrolyte, TEP, variable temperature

6. Caveats & Limitations

The 'dominant chemical shift' maps to different physical species across the coalescence, so its non-monotonic behavior and near-zero regression R^2 are expected and should NOT be interpreted as a continuous shift trend or an Arrhenius relation. No Larmor frequency was in the metadata: FWHM is reported in ppm only, precluding Hz conversion and T2* estimation, so exchange vs relaxation contributions to linewidth cannot be quantitatively separated from these five spectra alone. The mid-T dispersive S-shaped apex residual is left unresolved by the symmetric-Voigt model and is ambiguous between genuine near-coalescence asymmetry and a small phase error (phase correction was outside the locked constraint level) — this is a model-vs-evidence divergence that does not overturn the exchange interpretation but warrants re-phasing/refit. Only 5 of the stated 30 VT spectra are summarized here; coalescence temperature and exchange rates should be extracted from the full ladder plus the T1 relaxation data rather than asserted from this subset. Species assignments (free TEP vs Mg-coordinated TEP) are inherited from the model design and are chemically reasonable given the 31P shift range but are not independently verified here.
